name: Egg Shakshuka
steps: Gently cook the onion, peppers and garlic in the oil until soft.
Add the aubergine and brown it, then stir in tomatoes, purée, spices and salt and simmer until thick.
Add the chickpeas, then wilt in the spinach.
Make six hollows, crack in the eggs, cover and cook on low until the whites set.
Rest a minute, scatter with coriander and serve.
description: Eggs poached in a spiced tomato, aubergine and chickpea sauce - a big, veg-packed brunch.
whoItsFor: Vegetarians and anyone wanting a filling weekend brunch with plant and egg protein.
tips: Make the sauce ahead and reheat portions with fresh eggs on busy mornings.
Add a slice of wholemeal toast for extra carbs before a long session.
sourceNote: NHS Healthier Families recipe (© Crown copyright). Ingredient list copied as facts; method rewritten in Somax's own words. Nutrition per serving as published on the page.

name: Turkey Koftas with Minty Yoghurt
steps: Combine the turkey with the onion, carrot, garlic, cumin, purée, breadcrumbs and egg yolk.
Shape into eight sausages around the skewers.
Grill for 15-20 minutes, turning now and then, until cooked through.
Stir the mint into the yoghurt and dress the sliced tomato and red onion with oil and pepper.
description: Lean spiced turkey skewers with a cool mint yoghurt dip and tomato salad.
whoItsFor: People cutting calories who still want a satisfying, high-protein dinner.
tips: Serve with pitta or rice on training days for more carbs.
Double the batch - cooked koftas keep 3 days in the fridge.
sourceNote: NHS Healthier Families recipe (© Crown copyright). Ingredient list copied as facts; method rewritten in Somax's own words. Nutrition per serving as published on the page.

name: Pesto & Parmesan Salmon Traybake
steps: Roast the courgettes, onions and carrots with the oil and pepper at 200°C for about 30 minutes, stirring halfway.
Mix breadcrumbs, pesto, cheese and spread and press onto the salmon on a lined tray.
Bake the salmon with the veg for 15-20 minutes until the fish flakes.
Boil the potatoes for about 15 minutes and serve alongside.
description: Crumb-topped salmon roasted with vegetables and new potatoes - omega-3s and carbs in one tray.
whoItsFor: Endurance athletes and anyone wanting an easy, balanced post-training dinner.
tips: Great the evening after a long run or ride.
Swap new potatoes for sweet potato for variety.
sourceNote: NHS Healthier Families recipe (© Crown copyright). Ingredient list copied as facts; method rewritten in Somax's own words. Nutrition per serving as published on the page. The page lists kcal and fat only; protein and carbs are Somax estimates from the ingredients.

name: Turkey & Orange Stir-fry
steps: Soak the noodles in boiling water for about 6 minutes.
Whisk orange juice, soy sauce and cornflour; heat the oil in a wok.
Stir-fry the turkey for 3-4 minutes, add the veg and cook on high for another 3-4 minutes.
Add the sauce until it thickens, toss in the drained noodles and serve.
description: A fast, lean noodle stir-fry with a sticky orange-soy glaze.
whoItsFor: Busy people who need a 25-minute high-protein dinner.
tips: Use firm tofu for a vegetarian version.
Swap noodles for rice and pack leftovers for lunch.
sourceNote: NHS Healthier Families recipe (© Crown copyright). Ingredient list copied as facts; method rewritten in Somax's own words. Nutrition per serving as published on the page.

name: Panjabi Dhal
steps: Simmer the lentils in the water with turmeric and salt, part-covered, for about 15 minutes.
Fry the cumin seeds in the oil, then soften and brown the onion and garlic; add the chillies.
Stir the spiced onions into the lentils, bring to the boil, then take off the heat.
Top with coriander and serve with rice or chapatis.
description: A comforting, budget-friendly lentil dhal packed with plant protein and fibre.
whoItsFor: Vegans, vegetarians and anyone on a budget wanting a filling plant-based meal.
tips: Soak the lentils for a few hours to cut cooking time.
Serve with rice and yoghurt (or soya yoghurt) to boost protein.
sourceNote: NHS Healthier Families recipe (© Crown copyright). Ingredient list copied as facts; method rewritten in Somax's own words. Nutrition per serving as published on the page.

name: Tuna & Bean Lunchbox Salad
steps: Whisk the oil, lemon, herbs, mustard and pepper.
Fold in the chopped veg, beans and tuna.
Pack with the bread, or swap the bread for cold pasta.
description: A no-cook lunchbox salad of tuna, beans and crunchy veg in a lemony dressing.
whoItsFor: Office workers wanting a quick, portable, high-protein lunch.
tips: Make it the night before - it holds up well.
Add a full can of tuna for a 35g+ protein lunch.
sourceNote: NHS Healthier Families recipe (© Crown copyright). Ingredient list copied as facts; method rewritten in Somax's own words. Nutrition per serving as published on the page.

name: Porridge with Yoghurt & Berries
steps: Bring the oats and water to the boil in a non-stick pan, stirring.
Simmer gently for about 5 minutes.
Spoon into bowls and top each with yoghurt and berries.
description: Simple oat porridge topped with yoghurt and berries - slow-release carbs to start the day.
whoItsFor: Runners, cyclists and anyone training in the morning who needs steady energy.
tips: Eat 1-2 hours before an endurance session.
Stir in a scoop of protein powder or use Greek yoghurt to boost protein.
sourceNote: NHS Healthier Families recipe (© Crown copyright). Ingredient list copied as facts; method rewritten in Somax's own words. Nutrition per serving as published on the page.

name: Chicken Jalfrezi
steps: Brown the chicken in the oil with cumin, turmeric, chilli and half the salt; set aside.
Soften the onions until golden; blend or mash the tomatoes.
Add ginger, garlic and peppers, then the tomatoes and remaining spices.
Return the chicken with the chillies and water and simmer, covered, for 10-15 minutes.
Finish with coriander.
description: A punchy, high-protein chicken curry with peppers and chillies - lighter than a takeaway.
whoItsFor: Lifters wanting 40g of protein in a flavourful dinner; good for batch-cooking.
tips: Batch-cook and freeze in portions.
Serve with rice on heavy training days, extra veg on rest days.
sourceNote: NHS Healthier Families recipe (© Crown copyright). Ingredient list copied as facts; method rewritten in Somax's own words. Nutrition per serving as published on the page. The page's fat figure reads '79g', an apparent typo; 11g is a Somax estimate from the ingredients.

name: Potato & Poached Egg Hash
steps: Fry the bacon in the oil, add the potatoes and brown them.
Stir in the spring onions and tomatoes and keep warm on a low heat.
Poach the eggs in simmering water with a dash of vinegar.
Share the hash between plates, top with an egg and season.
description: Crispy potato and bacon hash topped with a runny poached egg.
whoItsFor: Anyone wanting a hearty weekend breakfast that uses up leftover potatoes.
tips: Cook extra potatoes at dinner to make this quick.
Add a second egg for more protein.
sourceNote: NHS Healthier Families recipe (© Crown copyright). Ingredient list copied as facts; method rewritten in Somax's own words. Nutrition per serving as published on the page.

name: Peppers with Spicy Turkey Stuffing
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C and sit the pepper halves in a roasting tin.
Cook the rice for 12-15 minutes and drain.
Soften onion and garlic, stir-fry the turkey, then add tomatoes, peas, paprika and herbs.
Mix in the rice, fill the peppers, cover with foil and bake for 20-25 minutes.
description: Roasted peppers stuffed with paprika turkey and rice - very low in fat.
whoItsFor: People in a fat-loss phase who want big portions for few calories.
tips: Fill and refrigerate in the morning, bake in the evening.
Use brown rice for extra fibre.
sourceNote: NHS Healthier Families recipe (© Crown copyright). Ingredient list copied as facts; method rewritten in Somax's own words. Nutrition per serving as published on the page.

name: Haddock Florentine
steps: Grill the haddock with the tomatoes for 5-6 minutes until the fish flakes.
Poach the eggs for 4-5 minutes and toast the bread.
Wilt the spinach by pouring boiling water over it in a colander, then drain.
Plate spinach, fish and egg; serve with the tomatoes and toast.
description: Grilled haddock on wilted spinach topped with a poached egg - 37g protein in 15 minutes.
whoItsFor: Anyone wanting a very fast, lean, high-protein meal.
tips: Works as a big post-workout brunch too.
Swap haddock for any white fish or salmon.
sourceNote: NHS Healthier Families recipe (© Crown copyright). Ingredient list copied as facts; method rewritten in Somax's own words. Nutrition per serving as published on the page.

name: Simple Rajma (Kidney Bean) Curry
steps: Fry the curry leaves, seeds, dried chilli and hing in hot oil until the seeds pop.
Add garlic, then tomatoes and the remaining spices; cook hard for 10 minutes.
Add the beans and hot water, cover and simmer for 15-20 minutes.
Stir in coriander and serve with rice, yoghurt and cucumber.
description: A fragrant North-Indian-style kidney bean curry served with rice - big on carbs and fibre.
whoItsFor: Vegetarians and endurance athletes needing a carb-rich, budget meal.
tips: Great the night before a long run or match.
Use soya yoghurt to make it vegan.
sourceNote: NHS Healthier Families recipe (© Crown copyright). Ingredient list copied as facts; method rewritten in Somax's own words. Nutrition per serving as published on the page.

name: Salmon & Broccoli Pasta
steps: Grill the salmon for 5-6 minutes and rest it.
Boil the pasta for 8 minutes, then add spring onions and broccoli for 3-4 more.
Drain over the peas, keeping 2 tbsp of the water.
Melt soft cheese and milk with the reserved water into a sauce; add lemon zest and herbs.
Return pasta and veg, flake in the salmon, season and top with cheese.
description: Creamy lemon-herb wholemeal pasta with flaked salmon, broccoli and peas.
whoItsFor: Active people who want a balanced carb-and-protein dinner in 30 minutes.
tips: Ideal after evening training.
Portion leftovers for next-day lunch - eat cold or reheat thoroughly.
sourceNote: NHS Healthier Families recipe (© Crown copyright). Ingredient list copied as facts; method rewritten in Somax's own words. Nutrition per serving as published on the page.

name: Greek Yoghurt & Raspberry Chill
steps: Toast the oats under the grill until golden and leave to cool.
Lightly mash half the raspberries.
Stir the yoghurt and oats through the mashed fruit.
Spoon into glasses, top with whole raspberries and chill.
description: A light, fruity yoghurt pot with toasted oats.
whoItsFor: Anyone wanting a sweet, low-calorie snack or dessert.
tips: Use 0% Greek yoghurt or skyr to double the protein.
Make 4 pots on Sunday for the week's snacks.
sourceNote: NHS Healthier Families recipe (© Crown copyright). Ingredient list copied as facts; method rewritten in Somax's own words. Nutrition per serving as published on the page.

name: Quick Chicken Couscous
steps: Pour the hot stock over the couscous and leave for 10-15 minutes.
Fluff with a fork.
Stir through the chicken, sweetcorn, tomato, cucumber, lemon and pepper.
description: A no-cook-really couscous salad with leftover roast chicken.
whoItsFor: Busy people wanting a fast lunchbox with protein and carbs for afternoon training.
tips: Use leftover roast chicken.
Keeps 2 days in the fridge - good meal-prep lunch.
sourceNote: NHS Healthier Families recipe (© Crown copyright). Ingredient list copied as facts; method rewritten in Somax's own words. Nutrition per serving as published on the page.

name: Turkey Burgers
steps: Mix the turkey, onion, carrot, sweetcorn, herbs and pepper and shape four burgers.
Grill for 12-15 minutes, turning once, until cooked through; rest briefly.
Toast the buns and build with lettuce, burger and tomato.
description: Juicy homemade turkey burgers with hidden veg - 38g protein each.
whoItsFor: Families and lifters wanting a fakeaway that fits their goals.
tips: Freeze uncooked patties between baking paper.
Use a lettuce wrap instead of a bun for fewer carbs.
sourceNote: NHS Healthier Families recipe (© Crown copyright). Ingredient list copied as facts; method rewritten in Somax's own words. Nutrition per serving as published on the page.

name: Tuna & Bean Jacket Potatoes
steps: Bake the pricked potatoes at 200°C for about an hour.
Mix the beans, tuna, veg, vinegar and purée and season.
Split the hot potatoes and pile in the filling.
description: Fluffy jacket potatoes with a zingy tuna and bean filling - almost no fat.
whoItsFor: Anyone wanting a cheap, filling, low-fat meal.
tips: Microwave the potatoes for 8-10 minutes then crisp in the oven to save time.
Use tofu for a vegetarian version.
sourceNote: NHS Healthier Families recipe (© Crown copyright). Ingredient list copied as facts; method rewritten in Somax's own words. Nutrition per serving as published on the page.

name: Scrambled Eggs on Mega-Mushrooms
steps: Grill the peppers and mushroom caps for 4-5 minutes, turning once.
Whisk the eggs with the milk.
Scramble the eggs with the chopped stalks in the melted spread, then fold in the peppers and tomatoes.
Serve on the mushroom caps with toasted pitta.
description: Fluffy scrambled eggs piled on grilled mushrooms with peppers and pitta.
whoItsFor: Vegetarians and anyone wanting a veg-heavy cooked breakfast.
tips: Add egg whites to bump protein without many calories.
Skip the pitta on rest days for a lower-carb plate.
sourceNote: NHS Healthier Families recipe (© Crown copyright). Ingredient list copied as facts; method rewritten in Somax's own words. Nutrition per serving as published on the page.
